Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacist applies Massachusetts’s six-month and five-refill limits to an ordinary Schedule V prescription.
A pharmacist fills a Schedule III refill after the six-month issue-date limit because the unused refill count is positive.
A receiving pharmacy accepts only drug name and today’s date as the complete III–V refill-transfer record.
Both pharmacies use two years from the first transfer as the only retention endpoint even when a later refill extends the required period.
A pharmacist records refill date, quantity, and dispensing pharmacist identification.

Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

choices.text: A pharmacist concludes that any product sold by the same company is the authorized generic of the prescribed brand.
During a qualifying medical emergency, a pharmacist documents the date, hour, and nature of the event and obtains written purchaser acceptance for the permitted substitution.
A pharmacist gives the patient the required written notification after an eligible biological substitution.
